newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money still below the special adv. rate.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money still below the special adv. rate.

text.p: Dutch call money rates were slightly higher on Monday compared to Friday, but remained on the low side.

Dealers said they expected call rates to stay at current levels for several days as the latest special advances allocation had been ample and call money was trading just below the pact's 2.90 percent rate.
Business was thin as market players were staying on the sidelines during the EMU summit in Amsterdam.
"By Wednesday it should be clear what the outcome of the summit is and business will catch up then," said one dealer.
Another dealer said call was currently lower than it had been in the previous weeks because market players were getting used to the new money market instruments, introduced on May 23.
"They had been playing on the safe side and saved more than they should have after the new instruments were introduced," said the dealer.
Since the introduction of the new instruments banks are no longer allowed to hold a negative balance with the central bank at the end of the day.
Banks with a negative balance have to fill the gap by borrowing at the marginal advance rate, currently 4.5 percent.
Call was bid at around 2.88 percent compared to 2.75-2.87 on Friday.
The guilder was hardly changed at 112.495 per 100 marks from 112.485 on Friday.
